criteria.name: Problem passes the swap-test
criteria.rationale: Names a specific customer and situation no competitor could claim word for word: "Marisol Vega, office manager at a six-therapist clinic" losing "six to eight patients a week... almost always the morning of," with the pain rendered concretely as "Four calls in it's one-thirty, the slot is gone, and she's stopped trying." The right-fit criteria (same therapist, same plan of care, "able to get to the clinic by two") are this clinic's, not a generic category.

criteria.name: Appetite is a fixed tier
criteria.rationale: The field reads "Small (≤2 weeks)" — the tier name carrying its standard fixed budget as a bound, not a duration the team estimated for this particular work. Rabbit Holes corroborates the fixed-budget framing by calling it "a two-week bet" that carrier approval could eat into, which is a tier being spent rather than a schedule being predicted.

criteria.name: Solution sketch under-specified and within cap
criteria.rationale: Roughly 80 words, well under the ~150 cap, with no diagrams, no acceptance criteria, and no edge-case enumeration. It actively declines specification — "No matching logic, no caseload scanning" — and the only concrete details (reply YES, thirty-minute window, offer moves down the list) are shape, not spec.

criteria.name: Every assumption passes the falsifiability checklist
criteria.rationale: The one assumption records all four sub-fields: a quantified claim ("Auto-offering a cancelled slot by text fills at least half of offered slots within the hour"), a pre-committed threshold ("Fewer than a quarter of offered slots claimed within an hour... roughly twelve to sixteen"), a cheap test ("founder texting from the list personally... About an hour of founder time total"), and a timebox ("By Friday 21 August 2026"). The threshold is genuinely failable — cold-texted waitlist patients claiming under 25% within an hour is a plausible real outcome, not a guaranteed pass.
